research_question: What do NPDB payment reports and AMA survey data show about medical malpractice in the United States, and what can they not prove?

research_brief.purpose: Owner-approved statistics page for medical malpractice statistics, rebuilt from the owner draft after a live fact-check.
research_brief.audience: Readers, students, journalists, and legal professionals in the United States who need sourced figures.
research_brief.data_period: NPDB cumulative counts as of December 2025; NPDB public use file through June 30, 2026 (August 2026 release); AMA Benchmark Surveys 2016-2022 (April 2023 study)
research_brief.scope_limitations: NPDB counts are payment reports, not claims or proven negligence. The statement that payments are not findings of negligence is labeled as our reading, not an NPDB statement. Public-file field details and payment-range claims in the owner draft were cut as unverified.

sources.title: What Is the NPDB?
sources.scope: ~1,354,000 adverse action reports; ~529,000 medical malpractice payment reports; ~45,000 judgment or conviction reports (as of Dec. 2025); 15.9 million plus query responses and 71,800 plus new reports in 2025; MMPR definition
sources.method: Opened and read the live page on 2026-11-10 (Claude fact-check); every figure used was matched to the page text; fact-check sign-off by Darlene Aberin.
sources.limitations: Administrative records; figures can be revised by the publisher. Not legal advice.

sources.title: Medical Liability Claim Frequency Among U.S. Physicians
sources.publisher: American Medical Association (José R. Guardado, PhD)
sources.scope: Benchmark Surveys 2016-2022: 31.2% ever sued (2022), 34.0% (2016); 1.8% sued prior year (2022); 61 claims per 100 physicians (2022), 68 (2016); 72% of claims no indemnity payment; 65% dropped/dismissed/withdrawn; 6% trial verdict, 89% defendant wins; OB/GYN 62.4%, general surgery 59.3% ever sued
sources.method: Downloaded the live PDF on 2026-11-10 and extracted its text (Claude fact-check); every figure used was matched to the text; fact-check sign-off by Darlene Aberin.
sources.limitations: Administrative records; figures can be revised by the publisher. Not legal advice.

sources.limitations: Administrative records; figures can be revised by the publisher. Not legal advice.

content_gaps: Pages treat NPDB payment reports as all malpractice cases.
Few pages explain that most claims pay nothing.
Specialty risk is rarely shown with a dated, nationally representative source.
value_add: Pairs NPDB payment counts with AMA survey claim frequency, shows closed-claim outcomes, separates payment, claim, and negligence, and documents public file coverage and timing caveats.
